newsitem.title: UK: LME chairman calls for greater market transparency.
newsitem.headline: LME chairman calls for greater market transparency.

text.p: Greater transparency, but not over-regulation, is required in any changes that are made following the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) review of the London Metal Exchange (LME), Raj Bagri, LME Board Chairman said.

There is no reason why this greater transparency of data should not be made available to all market participants and it might include details of position sizes, including options and warrants, Bagri said in a speech delivered at the LME's annual dinner.

Bagri said investigations that the LME made into the copper market prior to the unfolding of the Sumitomo Corp affair in June were frustrated by a lack of jurisdiction and information in the OTC and underlying cash markets.
Difficulties could partly be mitigated by the LME being provided details of OTC positions of LME members and their clients, along with details of their warrant holdings.
Also, any UK firm which actively trades on the LME should be required by the Financial Services Act to be an LME member.
This removes the opportunity for these companies to stay out of the LME's regulatory reach, Bagri said.
